forecaster_note: Fri: S swell drifts SE and eases, E swell builds; head high at S exposures, waist–chest elsewhere; persistent easterlies = lump and wobble, hard to find clean. Sat: short-period SSE/SE + mixed E swells, still onshore — lumpy but better than Fri; best early. Sun: SE/E mix, head high at S exposures, offshore and clean in the morning then onshore from mid-morning. Mon: peaky waist–chest, cleanish AM. — Surfline forecaster (Hugh McDowell), Fri 16 Oct

wind.summary: Onshore E ~15 kph (gusts ~25) at 6am, steady 15–19 kph E all day. Light showers early, brief showers around noon.

shark.summary: Northern Beaches (Palm Beach → Manly), last 24h: no shark detections at Palm Beach, Manly, Curl Curl, Dee Why or Long Reef. Feed is current (newest statewide detection ~1h ago, Birubi/Port Stephens; ~38 real detections statewide in 24h, all mid-north coast or north). DPI feed returned no features. Always check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: SSE 5.7ft @ 9s easing (~570 kJ) plus building small E swell. Persistent easterlies = lumpy, poor-fair. Long Reef/Curl Curl biggest (chest–OH); dawn only.
days.surfline_text: We're looking to see the S swell drift further SE and ease with some building E swell - head high or so for S exposures, about waist to chest elsewhere. It'll be hard to find anything clean though, with persistent easterly winds adding plenty of lump and wobble to the surf.

swells.label: SSE swell, 9s, ~521 kJ — drifting SE and easing; short period, wraps OK into Dee Why but lumpy

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Short-period SSE/SE + E swells, still onshore but better than Fri. Early morning is the shot; S magnets head high plus, elsewhere waist–chest.
days.surfline_text: Short period SSE/SE swell is joined by some mixed easterly swells. Sth magnets will still be picking up the most size - in the head high plus range. Most other beaches will be waist to chest. We're still going to be battling the onshore winds - best chance for something more appealing will be in the early morning and maybe at the very S facing breaks if we get a bit of N in the wind. I think it will be a fairly lumpy, but better than Friday.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sun is the better day: SE/E mix, offshore and clean in the morning, head high at S exposures, onshore and lumpy from mid-morning. Sat lumpy, early only. Mon peaky waist–chest, cleanish AM.
days.surfline_text: Short period SSE/SE swell is joined by some mixed easterly swells. Sth magnets will still be picking up the most size - in the head high plus range. Most other beaches will be waist to chest. We're still going to be battling the onshore winds - best chance for something more appealing will be in the early morning and maybe at the very S facing breaks if we get a bit of N in the wind. I think it will be a fairly lumpy, but better than Friday. SE and E swell mix should give us something head high at the south exposures with waist to chest at other breaks. Winds should go offshore in the morning with clean surf. Then going onshore and lumpy from mid to later morning.
